Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test expects StringUtils.newStringUtf8(null) and StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(null) to return null rather than throwing a NullPointerException.

Inspecting the implementation:
- StringUtils.newStringUtf8(byte[]) delegates to a shared helper:
  - newStringUtf8(bytes) -> newString(bytes, Charsets.UTF_8)
  - newString(byte[], Charset) returns bytes == null ? null : new String(bytes, charset)
  This path is null-safe and returns null for null input, satisfying the first assertion.

- StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(byte[]) directly constructs a new String without a null check:
  - return new String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1);
  If bytes is null, this throws a NullPointerException, causing the test to fail on the second assertion.

This inconsistency likely stems from the refactor to use Charset objects (referenced in the bug report): some methods were updated to use the null-safe helper, while newStringIso8859_1 (and possibly others) were not, resulting in a regression where null inputs now cause NPEs rather than returning null.
